label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hi D. Bergeron, and hi everybody. Yes, it's me, Hélène from Le Pétrin Doré. My nephew Thomas showed me this thread this morning, so here is the straight answer you asked for, and you are right to ask.

**We are not closing. We are not moving. We bought the building.**

I wanted to keep this as a surprise for the reopening, but I see the surprise made people worry, so I'll tell you everything now.

**The building**

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right. The building at the corner was sold. It was sold to me. 😊

Many of you know M. Ferland, who owned the building. He is 81 now and he is retiring to Sherbrooke to live near his daughter. Before he put it on the market, he came to me and offered to sell to me first, before anybody else. I didn't sleep for a few weeks, I talked to the bank many times, and we signed at the notary on December 15. M. Ferland cried a little bit at the notary. To be honest, me too.

For 17 years he came every morning for his baguette, "pas trop cuite," always the same. I will miss him at 7h15 every morning. If he comes to visit from Sherbrooke, the baguette is on me for life.

So there will be no condos, no bank and no vape shop. The bakery stays where it is, at 5 Fairmount on the corner, where it has been since March 2009.

**To the people who live upstairs**

I know some of you read this board, and I know you must have been worried too when you heard the building was sold. The 3 apartments stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent. I already promised this to each of you in writing, and I will keep that promise. You are my neighbours and I'm not going anywhere, and neither are you.

**Why we close January 4 to 18**

It's for works, not vacation (but Priya, thank you for defending my right to a vacation, haha).

Our deck oven is from 1998. It broke 3 times this year, and some of you were there the morning in September when there was no bread until 11h. Now that the building is mine, I can finally do things properly. A new 4-deck oven is coming from a supplier in Laval, and it needs those two weeks to be installed and tested. I am not opening with an oven I don't know yet.

There is also another nice thing. We are taking the space at the back, the old storage room of the dépanneur. We will put 6 small tables there. After 17 years of people eating their croissant standing on the sidewalk in February, **you can finally sit down.** It's small, but it's a start.

**We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7h**, same as always.

**About the shelves on the 28th**

The half-empty shelves had nothing to do with closing. We sold everything for Christmas Eve, 400 bûches, plus all the bread. Our team was dead tired on the 26th and 27th. Empty shelves in the last week of December are a very good sign for a bakery, I promise!

**About the sign**

I have to confess this one. Thomas wrote the sign at 6h in the morning, "Grande nouvelle bientôt!" was his idea, and I said ok without really thinking. He was excited and I was busy with the dough. Reading it now, I see very well how "closed + big news + building sold" looks like the end. It was not smart. That's my fault, not his, and I'm sorry for the worry.

**Now the carnets. I want to be very clear.**

In October we sold 214 carnets, $60 for 12 loaves. Here is everything you need to know:

- **Every carnet is still good.** All of them, every loaf left on them.
- **There is no expiry.** That was true in October and it's still true. Use them in January, in June, in 2030, it doesn't matter.
- **As a thank you, every carnet holder gets 1 free croissant in January** when they come in after the reopening. Just show your carnet.
- **If you want your money back, come see me and I give it back, no question.** I don't need an explanation, I won't be upset, and I won't argue. If the last two weeks made you lose confidence, I understand, and you can have your money for the loaves you have left.

noodle_and_crumb, your 7 loaves are waiting for you, and so is a croissant.

I will be honest about one thing. When I read the word "scam," it hurt. I have been on this street for 17 years. I know a lot of you by name, I know your kids, and I know who takes the pain de campagne sliced and who will be angry if I slice it. I understand why people worry, because Mile End lost a lot of small shops in the last years and every time a sign goes up we all think "here we go again." I feel it too when I walk on Saint-Laurent. So I'm not angry at anybody, really. I'm just glad I can tell you it's the opposite this time.

And D. Bergeron, you were fair with me. You asked a real question politely before the 4th, and you deserved a real answer. Thank you for that.

**Thank you**

Priya, thank you, and thank you to everybody who defended us here and in the shop the last few days. A few of you came in and said "I heard the rumour, I don't believe it," and that meant a lot to me. Priya, your kid can come see me for the chocolatine, the tradition continues.

jules_on_waverly, the pain de campagne is not going anywhere. In the new oven it will be even better, I hope.

**You are all invited!**

On **Saturday, January 23**, we are having a little reopening celebration. Everybody is welcome: regulars, new people, worried people, people who wrote on this board, people who didn't. **Free coffee and a piece of the new bread** from the new oven. Come see the new tables in the back, sit down for once, and tell me what you think of the bread.

I'll also try to convince M. Ferland to come down from Sherbrooke that day. We'll see.

So, to recap:
- Not closing, not moving, we bought the building
- Closed January 4 to 18 for the new oven and the new seating space
- Reopening Tuesday January 19 at 7h
- Carnets all valid, no expiry, free croissant in January, money back to anyone who wants it, no question
- Upstairs tenants stay with the same rent, promised in writing
- Party on Saturday January 23, with free coffee and bread for everybody

Thank you for caring this much about a little bakery. Honestly, that's the real "grande nouvelle" for me.

See you on the 19th,

Hélène
Le Pétrin Doré

P.S. Thomas says sorry for the sign. He's going to make the next one, but this time I'm reading it first. 😄
